messages:
maria: Noticing a recurring p99 spike on /api/generate around deploys this morning. App pod CPU shows exporter work as the top consumer in profiles.

metric-bot: [ALERT] route:/api/generate p99 >= 450ms in prod-us-west for 14m

jonathan: Did anything change in tracing libs or the collector config overnight?

lee: We updated otel SDK to 1.8 and switched the in-process exporter to OTLP/gRPC with gzip by default. Also enabled the new "debug_span_attrs" feature flag for a couple of services.

maria: Span volume increased ~1.8x after enabling the debug attrs. Many spans are short-lived middleware spans ~50-120B. pprof shows most time in proto marshaling and goroutine scheduling from many small export calls.

sam: Breakdown from the flamegraph: proto.Marshal ~42%, gzip compress ~10%, grpc send + stream scheduling ~28%, batching overhead ~12%, others ~8%.

lee: Current batch config in pod env:
```
OTLP_ENDPOINT=collector.prod:4317
OTEL_BSP_MAX_QUEUE_SIZE=2500
OTEL_BSP_MAX_EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE=200
OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY_MILLIS=400
OTEL_EXPORTER_COMPRESSION=gzip
```

jonathan: Large batch size + gzip + many tiny spans = heavy serialization CPU and GC churn. Also gRPC client uses multiple goroutines per in-flight RPC.

maria: Quick experiments on staging: switching to smaller batches reduced serialized time but increased syscall churn. Turning off compression dropped CPU, but network bytes increased ~2x.

sam: Three quick rollbacks we can apply that are low-risk:
- reduce MAX_QUEUE_SIZE to 600
- reduce EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE to 64
- disable debug_span_attrs feature flag (it inflates each span)

lee: Another option: push exporter to a sidecar process (dedicated sender) so app threads spend less time marshaling. Also test OTLP/HTTP with protobuf payload (fewer goroutines) and Snappy compression — cheaper CPU than gzip.

maria: Rolled the hotfix to prod-us-west-1: EXPORT_BATCH_SIZE=64, QUEUE_SIZE=600, DEBUG_SPANS=false. Early telemetry: exporter CPU down ~30% and route p99 dropped ~120ms within 2m.

deploy-bot: [DEPLOY] hotfix: telemetry-batch-adjust applied to service/api-generate @prod-us-west-1

metric-bot: [METRIC] exporter_cpu_pct prod-us-west-1 from 68% -> 47% (2m after change)

jonathan: Nice. Let's follow up with a structured benchmark matrix:
- OTLP/gRPC gzip vs OTLP/gRPC snappy vs OTLP/HTTP protobuf (no compression) vs OTLP/HTTP protobuf+snappy
- sidecar exporter vs in-process exporter
- GOGC tuning (baseline vs GOGC=100 vs GOGC=200) to see GC effect on p99

lee: I'll prototype the sidecar sender and a Snappy encoder. Early expectation: snappy trades bandwidth for much lower CPU. Sidecar should reduce app p99 by isolating serialization work.

sam: I'll add a temporary telemetry quota: span/min per service for debug-tier services and a client-side circuit-breaker that drops debug spans once quota exceeded. Also will add dashboard panels to break exporter time into marshal vs network.

maria: K6 load test scheduled against staging now. I'll capture heap+cpu pprof and flamegraphs for each variant and post links.

jonathan: Long-term ideas: per-span-value routing (route low-value spans to cold tier with lower retention), adaptive batching that splits if marshal time exceeds threshold, and an opt-in debug-span sampler that rate-limits debug emissions.

lee: Agree. Assignments:
- maria: run the benchmark matrix and upload profiles
- lee: sidecar + snappy prototype
- sam: temp quota + dashboard split
- jonathan: write follow-up RFC for adaptive batching and per-span routing

maria: TL;DR: debug attrs + big gzip batches caused CPU & GC pressure. Hotfix reduced batch and disabled debug attrs; p99 improved. Next: benchmark snappy/http/sidecar, implement quota/gating, and RFC adaptive batching. Posting pprof links in #eng-platform in ~40m.

jonathan: If p99 climbs back above 400ms after follow-ups, label incident telemetry-regress and open a postmortem.

maria: will do. Thanks all.
